ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, this is the creative physics experiment design work “Little Bear Swinging on a Swing.” Two metal rods C and D that are close to each other and insulated from each other are fixed on an iron stand, and form a closed circuit with two copper coils P and Q. Two very strongly magnetic bar magnets are placed as shown in the figure. When coil P is swung left and right by hand, coil Q also swings along with it, as if the little bear is swinging on a swing. Which of the following statements is correct? (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Multi-Physics open-ended question 1
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, when coil P is swinging to the right, what is the direction of the current in P (viewed from right to left)?

matched_variant_raw.title: Multi-Physics open-ended question 1
matched_variant_raw.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, when coil P is swinging to the right, what is the direction of the current in P (viewed from right to left)?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, when coil P is swinging to the right, what is the direction of the current in P (viewed from right to left)?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: in the figure, there is a horizontally placed bar magnet on the left side, and the end close to coil P is marked “S”; coil P is located to the right of this S pole and is adjacent to it; the problem states that coil P swings to the right, so P is moving away from the S pole of the left magnet. Reasoning: when P moves away from the S pole, the magnetic flux through P decreases. According to Lenz's law, the magnetic field produced by the induced current in P must hinder this moving away, so the face of P close to the magnet should form an N pole, so as to attract the S pole of the magnet. When one face of a coil is an N pole, the current is counterclockwise when viewed from that face; but the problem requires “viewed from right to left,” that is, viewed from the side of P facing away from the magnet, and the direction is exactly opposite, so the observed current direction is clockwise.
